learning_outcomes.text: Understand the specific technical structure and the theoretical-technical bases, as well as the key concepts and aspects, of metrology.
Have adequate knowledge of the fundamentals of metrology, including the contribution of cutting-edge scientific knowledge to the development of this science.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve measurement chain design problems.
Have an understanding of the different methods for calculating uncertainties of a measurement system and the ability to use them.
Be able to design measurement chains and conduct experimental tests, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Possess technical and laboratory skills in machine testing.
Be able to select and use appropriate measurement equipment for the specific objectives of an experimental test.
Have an understanding of applicable testing methods and techniques in machine testing and their limitations.
Work effectively both individually and in a team.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering field.
Adequate knowledge of their engineering field, including some cutting-edge knowledge.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory skills.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
Understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component, or process in the field of mechanical engineering, to meet required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design, and testing of machines.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology, and quality control.

syllabus_topics: 2.3. Fundamental concepts of a measurement chain.
Topic 4: Design of a Measurement Chain
Topic 5: Experimental techniques in mechanical engineering: extensometry. Application to fatigue test monitoring
5.2. RECOMMENDATIONS, PROCEDURES AND CRITERIA FOR STRAIN GAUGE SELECTION
5.3. SURFACE PREPARATION FOR STRAIN GAUGE ADHESION
Topic 6: Experimental techniques in mechanical engineering: photoelasticity.
6.1.1.2. Representative curves of a plane elastic state: Isostatics, Isoclines, Isochromatics
6.2. INTRODUCTION TO STRESS ANALYSIS WITH THE PHOTOSTRESS METHOD
Practice No. 1: Experimental methods in mechanical engineering. Determination, using extensometric techniques, of stresses and strains of a mechanical element.
Practice No. 2: Experimental methods in mechanical engineering. Determination, using photoelastic techniques, of stresses and strains of a mechanical element.
assessment_rules: The final exam accounts for 30% of the final grade. The rest of the evaluation (70%) corresponds to the mandatory work developed by the student during the course. Attendance at practical sessions and submission of the corresponding practical work are mandatory conditions to be eligible for the exam. The mandatory work can be done in groups of two students and includes a report and a 15-minute PowerPoint presentation.
